decisions.reason: The existing same-message MODIFY already adds the SK6812 LEDs to the complete 3.3V rail powered in standalone USB mode.
Moving the LEDs from 5V to 3.3V does not remove either monitored rail or change the monitor device, position, or stated measurement coverage.
The current 5V_EN function incorrectly ties switching the 5V rail to LED demand; the source necessarily makes that LED-specific description obsolete because the LEDs now use 3.3V.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: The LEDs are now powered from 3.3V instead of 5V. At 3.3V supply the SK6812 data threshold drops to 2.31V, which the ESP32 3.3V output satisfies directly, so no level shifter is needed. The tradeoff is that 3.3V is slightly below the SK6812 datasheet minimum (3.7V), but it works reliably at indicator brightness levels.

value_updates.five_v_enable_signal_function: Carries 5V_EN control for the switchable 5V rail; the SK6812 LEDs are no longer powered from that rail

decisions.reason: The existing same-message MODIFY already removes the SK6812 LEDs from the 5V powered loads and deletes the obsolete LED-specific standby policy.
AXP2101 remains the normal-operation source covering all system loads; only the downstream rail supplying the LEDs changes.
The existing same-message MODIFY fully records the 3.3V supply, direct ESP32 data drive, accepted below-datasheet voltage constraint, and removal of the obsolete level-shifter part.
The charge-status display can continue using the SK6812 chain unchanged; its electrical supply and data interface are owned by the separate addressable-LED Requirement.
The LED supply decision does not alter the panel button connector, PWRON connection, board location, or control behavior.
The LED rail change does not affect battery protection, cutoff voltages, or DW01A protection components.
The LED rail change does not affect the battery NTC connector or thermal-protection behavior.
The LED supply decision does not resolve or modify the battery connector family, part, pin functions, or unresolved pin order.

The daughterboard already specifies a 3.3V supply, while the newly confirmed threshold and level-shifting semantics are represented by the separate addressable-LED power and data-interface Requirement.
